name: FIFA Panini Collection
summary: FIFA Panini Collection digitizes sticker collecting for the FIFA World Cup 2026: packs opened from a held count reveal players that get glued into an album with one slot per player, duplicates go to a swap stack, and a Coca-Cola partnership runs through scanning, the packs and a whole badge category. A guest can play with reduced daily allowances before registering through a FIFA.com account unlocks the full set of packs, swap requests and challenges. A $2 deluxe pack and two purchase-count rewards are the only paid routes, both converging on a keepsake album sold outside the app, and the whole collection is available only until 30 September 2026.
teaser: FIFA Panini Collection states every guest limit as an exact number next to what registering would unlock, before asking the user to choose.

observations.name: Privacy notice first
observations.observed: On opening, FIFA Panini Collection shows a privacy notice stating that it values the user's privacy and, with trusted partners, collects certain personal data for a more personalized experience, with a link to read more and a Let's start button. The screen carries illustrations of Canada, Mexico and the United States, the tournament's three host countries, alongside three mascots. No decline option is described; tapping Let's start is the only route forward shown.

observations.name: Tracking and privacy prompts
observations.observed: After Let's start, FIFA Panini Collection requests permission to track the user's activity across other companies' apps and websites, using the name FIFA Panini, followed by a privacy settings pop-up. FIFA Panini Collection doesn't state what was chosen on either prompt.

observations.name: Sticker download screen
observations.observed: The app shows a downloading stickers state, then a screen showing the album with stickers outside it and two buttons, Resume your game and Start playing.

observations.name: Guest versus account choice
observations.observed: After Start playing, FIFA Panini Collection presents a screen headed to unlock the full experience by connecting an account, with two options side by side. Connecting with FIFA for free lists starting with three packs, two free packs every day, opening four packs a day, creating three swap requests, participating in challenges, promo codes and forming a collector's team. Being a guest lists starting with one pack, one free pack a day, opening one pack a day and creating one swap request, with challenges, promo codes and the collector's team all left off that list. Every allowance on this screen is stated as a number before the user chooses.

tags.name: Energy
tags.confidence: O8 (tier: directly observed); O10 (tier: plausible)
confidences: O8 (tier: directly observed); O10 (tier: plausible)
tags.rationale: The app maintains a per-day opening allowance, one for a guest and four for a registered account, that each opening consumes, that blocks further opening at zero while packs remain held, and that is stated to return after 15 hours (tier: directly observed). The concurrent swap-request cap behaves as a capacity occupied by each open request (tier: plausible, the cap and its account tiers are shown, but whether a slot is freed when a request ends was not seen). Exclusion conditions were checked first: the allowance is not a timer on one action, since it counts units across openings, and it is not removed by failure (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: For O10, a plain limit on open listings that is not a consumed capacity; it would stand if a slot were never released until the request completed (tier: plausible). Evidence that would separate them: a request withdrawn and a new one created at the cap.

tags.name: Daily Login Rewards
tags.confidence: O39 (tier: strongly supported); O4 (tier: directly observed)
confidences: O39 (tier: strongly supported); O4 (tier: directly observed)
tags.rationale: The account choice screen states one free pack every day for a guest and two for a FIFA account, and a "Get a free pack" control granted a pack on a tap with no task attached (tier: directly observed). The link between that control and the daily promise rests on the narrator's identification and on it being the only free-pack control described (tier: strongly supported). The daily reset itself was not observed and is recorded as behavior detail not seen. Exclusion conditions were checked first: no substantive task is required, and the grant is not the Coca-Cola scan, which requires a product in front of the camera (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: A one-time promotional free pack placed in the promo code area; it would stand if the control did not return the next day (tier: plausible). Evidence that would separate them: the same control offering a pack on a later day.

observations.name: Guest setup
observations.observed: Choosing to play as a guest opens a welcome screen asking for a country of residence. The notification permission request follows this screen.

observations.name: First home screen
observations.observed: The guest arrives on a home screen with a stadium background and five main items: Scan content, My stickers, My album, Open packs and Promo code, with Challenges, Swap area, My team and More in the bottom navigation. A banner promotes the deluxe pack's exclusive poster stickers. No tutorial or guided step runs between the guest setup and this screen. More opens a menu listing the public profile, collection rewards, prizes, rules, sharing, account settings, FAQs, completing the account, terms, privacy, accessibility and credits.

observations.name: Opening a pack
observations.observed: The Open packs item states how many unopened packs the user holds. Tapping it opens a pack, swiped open, revealing stickers of album players with a control to share them. Different openings produce different players, and a pack granted by scanning wasn't opened at the moment of the scan, only showing up later in the Open packs count.

tags.name: Loot Box
tags.confidence: O7 (tier: directly observed); O36 (tier: strongly supported)
confidences: O7 (tier: directly observed); O36 (tier: strongly supported)
tags.rationale: The app gives the user discrete packs held as a count and consumed on opening, and different openings resolve to different players (tier: directly observed). The user surrenders a held pack, and a unit of the daily opening allowance, before the contents are known (tier: directly observed). Loot Box is a specialization of Variable Reward Outcome; the specialization is reported and the parent is noted, following the overlap rule. The deluxe pack is a real-money container whose copy guarantees categories and missing items but does not name the stickers (tier: directly observed). Its opened contents were not seen because no purchase was made (tier: strongly supported, the offer copy establishes the unresolved contents while the purchase and reveal are absent). Exclusion conditions were checked first: the free packs are not opened by viewing an advertisement, and their contents are not fixed by a visible rule (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Variable Reward Outcome alone for the free packs, on the reading that a free pack involves no value commitment; rejected because the pack is a held entitlement that is consumed on opening, which the entry's earned-key variant covers (tier: strongly supported). Evidence that would separate them: packs that open automatically on grant, with no held count.

observations.name: Daily opening limit
observations.observed: As a guest, after opening one pack, FIFA Panini Collection blocks the next with a message stating a guest can open only one pack a day, that 15 hours remain, and inviting the user to complete their account to open more. After registering, the same block appeared after four openings, stating the daily limit had been reached. The allowance limits opening only; held packs beyond it simply wait.

observations.name: Gluing stickers in
observations.observed: My stickers shows the user's stickers in stacks, with instructions to move stickers between stacks, glue new ones into the album or swap them with other players. A red star marks each sticker not yet in the album. Dragging a sticker toward the album opens it at the matching player's page, with a plus button placing it on tap. Dragging a sticker to the swap stack instead makes it available for a swap request.

Gluing a missing player fills that player's slot, while duplicates stay in the stacks and go to swaps (tier: directly observed). Completion states are recognized at more than one level: the whole album, all cosmic stickers, and a count of completed teams on the achievements page (tier: directly observed). observations.name: Swap request cap
observations.observed: In the swap area, a guest sees a banner stating that a guest can create only a single swap request, and that completing the account allows up to three running at a time. After registration, two further slots for creating swap requests appear. The cap counts requests running at a time, a limit on concurrent open requests rather than a daily one. Dragging an offered sticker back to My stickers disables its swap request.

observations.name: Rules and FAQ
observations.observed: The Rules page presents the game as FIFA Panini Collection, powered by The Coca-Cola Company, a web and mobile application enhancing FIFA World Cup 26 based on the classic sticker album, available on Google Play and the App Store. It lists topics covering getting started, extra packs, opening packs, managing sticker stacks and albums, swapping, challenges, achievements, cosmic stickers, the dream team and support, with an FAQ reachable from inside the app. The contents of each topic aren't read out.

observations.name: The album itself
observations.observed: My album opens the virtual album, browsable by swiping or by a country-searchable index. Each player has a slot for their country, filled only when glued. The public profile reports album completion as a percentage, the number of stickers collected and the number of glued cosmic stickers. Cosmic stickers are holographic versions of regular stickers that glue into the same slot. The album includes poster pages for the hosting cities, and its index includes a Dream Team entry, with the achievements page as its last page.

observations.name: Collection rewards
observations.observed: The Collection rewards page lists four rewards. Two are tied to the album: completing 100% gives a personalized recap animation marked coming soon, and gluing every cosmic sticker gives a full discount coupon on a digital keepsake album. The other two are tied to deluxe pack purchases. No partial-completion reward is listed.

tags.name: Purchase Ladder
tags.confidence: directly observed, the offer screen shows the purchase count at zero and the two rewards, and the rewards page ties them to 20 and 25 purchases
confidences: directly observed, the offer screen shows the purchase count at zero and the two rewards, and the rewards page ties them to 20 and 25 purchases
tags.rationale: The app places two rewards at stated purchase counts of a repeatable offer, shows the user's count of purchased deluxe packs, and reveals both positions before any purchase (tier: directly observed). No progression measure advanced by play moves the count; only deluxe purchases do (tier: directly observed). The Prizes page's wording "upon obtaining" leaves open whether deluxe packs obtained otherwise count, recorded as not established (tier: unresolved). Exclusion conditions were checked first: the positions are not released by play, so this is not Progression Fund; the benefit depends on a cumulative count rather than the first purchase, so this is not First-Purchase Bonus (tier: directly observed).

observations.name: Achievement badges
observations.observed: The album's last page is headed to collect stickers and earn badges, listing seven categories each with three tiers: album progress, teams completed, challenges completed, team captains, swaps, previous World Cup winners, and Coca-Cola items scanned. The public profile carries its own achievements section, reading no big achievements yet for the guest. No reward is listed against any individual badge, and none was attained in this analysis.

observations.name: The three challenges
observations.observed: After registration, the Challenges screen reads that completing challenges earns rewards, and shows three numbered challenges. The first, on the hosting countries, rewarded the official mascots and is marked expired. The second rewarded a digital power pack for collecting five stickers of the last World Cup's winning team, also expired. The third, on team captains, rewards a Panini logo sticker for ten captains, shows zero of ten progress and two days remaining. A sticker must be in the album and clicked to count toward this challenge, and a participate button must be tapped to join. Expired challenges stay listed. The account screens describe challenges as weekly; guests can't open the Challenges screen at all, meeting a registration prompt instead.

observations.name: Locked-feature prompts
observations.observed: As a guest, tapping My team, Challenges or the promo code entry opens a prompt to register. Tapping to get the deluxe pack opens a pop-up stating that completing the account unlocks all features. Held packs beyond the guest's daily allowance can't be opened, with the same message directing the user to complete their account. Each prompt appears at the moment the guest tries to use the locked feature, and can be closed to return to the home screen.

tags.confidence: directly observed, team creation, the ID and password join rule, member completion and the team-only swap request type are all shown
confidences: directly observed, team creation, the ID and password join rule, member completion and the team-only swap request type are all shown
tags.rationale: The app maintains a named team with an ID, a password and a slogan, joined only with the ID and password, capped at 10 friends, with leave and invite controls (tier: directly observed). Membership changes a product condition: only members can create a collector's group swap request (tier: directly observed). Under the sibling decision ladder, no collective group-owned state was observed; member completion is shown per member and no team total, rank or reward appeared, so the most specific observed level is maintained membership and governance (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Clan / Guild; it would apply if the team held a group-level state such as a combined completion figure or team reward (tier: plausible). Evidence that would separate them: a team with several members showing a team total or ranking.

observations.name: Complete-account benefits
observations.observed: Continuing from the deluxe pack pop-up opens a screen titled completing the account to unlock the full game experience, listing three additional free packs per FIFA account, promo codes, weekly challenges, forming a collector's team, and more benefits, with buttons for an existing account or registering. Complete account is also a permanent entry in the More menu.

observations.name: Owned-sticker details
observations.observed: Tapping a player in the album shows details only for players whose sticker the user has: name, sticker, date of birth, height, weight, position and current club, with a share control. For one player, Irving Lozano, a button under the stats opens two historic stickers from previous competitions. FIFA Panini Collection doesn't establish whether every player has historic stickers available the same way.

observations.name: Availability end date
observations.observed: The screen reached by tapping to get new packs states that FIFA Panini Collection will be available until September 30, 2026. The statement applies to the whole collection, not to one offer. FIFA Panini Collection doesn't state what happens to the album and held packs after that date.

observations.name: Account settings
observations.observed: Account settings and preferences offers language choice, the account state, audio settings, a route for sticker image problems including redownloading assets, competition and privacy preferences reached through a consent center, and a Manage Preferences button, which for the guest reported no preferences to manage.

observations.name: Held packs and sources
observations.observed: FIFA Panini Collection holds unopened packs as a single count on the Open packs item. Packs enter that count from scanning the physical album, packs or a Coca-Cola can, the promo code area's free pack, and bonus packs granted on sign-up, with further sources listed as promo codes, QR codes, challenge rewards and deluxe pack purchases. Opening is the only way a pack leaves the count. The count can exceed the daily opening allowance, so packs wait unopened across days.

observations.name: Scanning the physical album
observations.observed: Scan content opens a screen inviting the user to unlock extra content with the camera, offering three buttons: scanning the FIFA World Cup album and packs, scanning Coca-Cola products, and scanning stickers from Coca-Cola. Choosing one requests camera access. Pointing the camera at the physical album shows a search state, then a check mark and an unlock free pack button; unlocking shows a congratulations message with the reward and a share control. observations.name: Scanning Coca-Cola products
observations.observed: Scanning Coca-Cola products asks the user to place a special Coca-Cola bottle in front of the camera and tap unlock once recognized. A different can was recognized the same way, but unlocking then stated the day's bonus for that item had already been claimed. The third option, scanning a special sticker from Coca-Cola, wasn't tried. The Coca-Cola scan reward is limited per day, though FIFA Panini Collection doesn't settle whether the limit is one total or one per product type.

observations.observed: Coca-Cola appears on three of the home screen items, as an advertising display, a Coca-Cola stand, and surrounding the packs, and the rules describe the collection as powered by The Coca-Cola Company. No benefit is attached to viewing the branding itself.

observations.name: FIFA.com registration
observations.observed: Register opens a FIFA.com login or sign-up screen stating that FIFA shares certain account information with Panini to operate the game and fulfil rewards, and that continuing links the FIFA.com account to FIFA Panini Collection. Continuing moves to the FIFA website. Sign-up runs three steps: date of birth, name, email, country, gender and communication language; a nickname seen by other users, a favourite team and consent to FIFA communication; then a password, followed by a registration code sent by email. No Google, Apple or other third-party sign-up route is offered on this screen. The verification email didn't arrive in this analysis; the link was reported expired, and creating the account again returned that the user already exists. The sign-in screen did offer a Google route, which was used to log in. Registration happened after the guest had already explored the home screen, scanned, opened a pack and created a swap request, not during first launch.

observations.name: Post-login consent
observations.observed: After login, FIFA Panini Collection shows a preferences screen with two statements. The first, required, confirms having read and accepted the terms of the prize promotion Complete the FIFA Panini Collection. The second, optional, consents to Panini sharing gaming data with FIFA for linked features, analytics and personalized experiences, withdrawable at any time.

observations.name: Share routes
observations.observed: Share controls appear on stickers revealed from a pack, the scan reward screen, a sticker's detail view, each challenge, the public profile, the dream team, the game itself, and the collector's team through Invite friends, sending a link through social media or messaging apps. No reward for sharing or inviting is stated anywhere in this analysis, and FIFA Panini Collection doesn't describe what a recipient of a shared sticker, challenge or profile actually sees.

observations.name: Rewards redeemed outside
observations.observed: Several rewards are fulfilled outside the app: a code for ten printed copies of a MyPanini sticker ordered on an external website with shipping not included, and discount codes on the digital keepsake album secured in the Panini America Blockchain Hub. The 100%-completion recap animation is the only collection reward described as delivered inside the app itself.

systemView: This is a medium system. Its spine is the pack: every source of stickers in the app, whether scanning, a daily claim, sign-up or a challenge reward, arrives as an unopened pack in one held count, and opening one is the only way stickers reach the album. A daily allowance sits between the held count and the album, capping only how many packs can be opened rather than how many can be held, and registering through a FIFA.com account raises every one of the app's allowances at once rather than unlocking separate features one at a time.

mechanicWriteups.name: Loot Box
mechanicWriteups.summary: Packs held as a count resolve into different players on opening, and a $2 deluxe pack guarantees categories of stickers without naming them.
mechanicWriteups.observed: FIFA Panini Collection holds packs as a count the user opens by swiping, and different openings produce different players. A $2 deluxe pack promises nine missing cosmic stickers, one missing poster sticker, and ten regular stickers that can include duplicates, without naming which stickers these will be.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Regular packs sit on the Open packs item as a running count, opened one at a time. The deluxe pack is promoted through a home screen banner and a dedicated offer screen stating its guaranteed categories before purchase.
mechanicWriteups.noting: FIFA Panini Collection guarantees the deluxe pack's categories rather than its contents; missing items are promised within those categories without saying which ones, so the same uncertainty running through the free packs also runs through the paid one.
findings: Regular packs are held as a count and opened one at a time, each producing different players.
The deluxe pack costs $2 and promises nine missing cosmic stickers, one missing poster sticker and ten regular stickers.
Deluxe pack copy guarantees categories, not which specific stickers will be received.
No purchase was made, so the deluxe pack's actual resolved contents aren't part of this record.

mechanicWriteups.name: Energy
mechanicWriteups.summary: A daily allowance limits how many packs can be opened, one for a guest and four registered, with a separate, less-established limit on open swap requests.
mechanicWriteups.observed: FIFA Panini Collection blocks further pack opening once the day's allowance is used, one opening for a guest and four for a registered account, stating a wait of about 15 hours before the next opening. Held packs beyond that allowance simply wait; opening is the only thing capped. The swap area separately states a cap on how many swap requests can run at once, one for a guest and three for a registered account.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The opening block appears as a message the moment the allowance runs out, naming the wait and inviting the user to complete their account for a higher daily limit. The swap cap appears as a banner in the swap area stating the same guest-versus-registered contrast.
mechanicWriteups.noting: FIFA Panini Collection states the swap-request cap in the same guest-versus-registered terms as the opening allowance, but only the opening allowance's return is actually shown; whether a swap slot frees up when a request is matched or withdrawn isn't something this write-up can describe.
findings: Pack opening is capped at one per day for a guest and four for a registered account.
The block message states a wait of about 15 hours rather than a clock time.
Holding packs isn't capped, only opening them; packs can accumulate across days.
A separate, stated cap of one open swap request for a guest and three for a registered account exists in the swap area.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the pack-opening limit message stating the wait; the swap area banner stating its request cap.

mechanicWriteups.name: Set Collection
mechanicWriteups.summary: An album with one slot per player tracks completion as a percentage, with duplicates routed to a swap stack instead.
mechanicWriteups.observed: FIFA Panini Collection gives every player a slot in a virtual album, filled only once its sticker is glued in; unglued stickers carry a red star. The public profile reports album completion as a percentage, alongside the number of stickers collected and cosmic stickers glued. Completing 100% of the album promises a personalized recap animation, marked as coming soon, and gluing every cosmic sticker unlocks a full discount coupon on a digital keepsake album sold outside the app.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Dragging a sticker toward the album opens it at the matching player's page, with a plus button over the empty slot. Completion figures sit on the public profile; the two completion rewards are listed on a dedicated Collection rewards page.
mechanicWriteups.noting: FIFA Panini Collection recognizes completion at more than one level at once, the whole album and the cosmic-sticker subset separately, each with its own named reward, rather than treating the album as a single finish line.
findings: Each player has a slot filled only when the matching sticker is glued in.
Unglued stickers are marked with a red star.
The public profile states album completion as a percentage alongside stickers collected and cosmic stickers glued.
Completing 100% of the album promises a recap animation marked coming soon; gluing every cosmic sticker unlocks a full discount coupon on an outside keepsake album.

The first two, tied to the hosting countries and the reigning champion team, are marked expired. sectionLeadIns.onboarding: FIFA Panini Collection asks for tracking and notification permissions before offering a choice between playing as a guest and registering through a FIFA account. This section covers that opening sequence through to the first unguided home screen.
sectionLeadIns.core-loop: Opening a pack is the one action every source of stickers in FIFA Panini Collection leads to. This section covers pack opening, the daily limit on it, and how a sticker moves from a pack into the album or a swap request.
sectionLeadIns.goals: FIFA Panini Collection tracks the album's own completion alongside a separate badge page and a set of time-limited challenges. This section covers all three.
sectionLeadIns.access: A guest's limits, the features locked behind registration, and what registering through FIFA.com actually asks for all sit in this section.
sectionLeadIns.economy: FIFA Panini Collection holds two things: packs waiting to be opened, and the stickers those packs produce, split between the album and a swap stack. This section covers where packs come from and how stickers move once they're out.
sectionLeadIns.social: FIFA Panini Collection's social layer runs through a matched swap system and a private team of friends. This section covers both, along with the public profile and dream team each exposes.
sectionLeadIns.reach: Scanning physical products, sharing controls placed on nearly every screen, and registering through a FIFA.com account are FIFA Panini Collection's three routes beyond its own screens. This section covers all three, along with the rewards that get fulfilled outside the app entirely.
sectionLeadIns.monetization: A single $2 deluxe pack and two rewards tied to a running purchase count are FIFA Panini Collection's only paid routes.
sectionLeadIns.returns: A notification request arriving before the home screen, and a free pack claimed once a day, are FIFA Panini Collection's two return mechanisms.

sectionCards.onboarding: A privacy notice, tracking and notification requests, and a guest-versus-account choice run before the guest reaches an unguided home screen.
sectionCards.core-loop: Opening a pack reveals players that get glued into the album or routed to a swap stack, bounded by a daily opening allowance and a cap on open swap requests.
sectionCards.goals: An album tracked by completion percentage, a tiered achievement badge page, and three numbered challenges all track progress at once.
sectionCards.access: A guest's allowances, feature locks and the registration path through a FIFA.com account all set what the rest of the app opens up.
sectionCards.economy: Packs held as a count, and stickers split between an album stack and a swap stack, are the two things FIFA Panini Collection actually holds.
sectionCards.social: A public swap system the app matches on its own, and a private team of up to ten friends, are the two ways other players enter the app.
sectionCards.reach: Scanning physical Coca-Cola products and Panini packaging, sharing routes on nearly every screen, and registration through FIFA.com are FIFA Panini Collection's three routes beyond its own screens.
sectionCards.monetization: A $2 deluxe pack and two purchase-count rewards are the only paid routes, both converging on a keepsake album sold outside the app.
sectionCards.returns: A daily free pack and a notification permission requested before the home screen are FIFA Panini Collection's two return mechanisms.

proposedTags.name: Matched Swap Request
proposedTags.draftDefinition: A matched swap request lets a user post a standing offer to exchange specified items from their own holdings for specified items they lack, and the product, rather than the user, searches other users' requests for a counterpart and completes or proposes the reciprocal exchange when one is found.
proposedTags.conditions: Items that can be transferred between users; a collection that produces duplicates; a pool of other users with open requests; a limit on how many requests one user can hold open.
proposedTags.whyNotCovered: Gifting excludes reciprocal exchanges. Set Collection lists trading only as a non-required condition of the collection. Group Membership covers the team scope of some requests but not the exchange itself.
proposedTags.recurrenceElsewhere: The pattern is described in general terms that apply to any product where users hold duplicate collectible items; no other analysis in this workspace was consulted to confirm it.
proposedTags.caveat: Held open. No match and no completed exchange were observed, so whether the exchange completes automatically or asks the user to confirm is not established, and that is the mechanic itself rather than a detail around it. Two pieces of evidence would settle it: a session that posts a request and sees it matched, showing what the product does at the moment a counterpart is found; and a second app carrying the same shape, a product-run search of other users' standing offers that completes or proposes the reciprocal exchange.

proposedTags.name: Product Scan Reward
proposedTags.draftDefinition: A product scan reward grants an in-product benefit when the user points the device camera at a recognized physical item, such as a sponsor's product or a physical edition of the product's own content, with the grant limited per item or per period.
proposedTags.conditions: Camera access; physical items the product can recognize; a benefit held in the product; a limit on repeat scans.
proposedTags.whyNotCovered: Rewarded Advertisement excludes benefits granted for using or purchasing the promoted offering. Earning Tasks requires disclosed effort, a catalogue separate from the core activity and a continuation layer. Daily Login Rewards requires access alone.
proposedTags.recurrenceElsewhere: Stated in general terms applicable to products tied to physical goods or packaging; no other analysis in this workspace was consulted to confirm it.
proposedTags.caveat: Held open. In this app the scan sits inside a sponsorship, and a commercial arrangement is not a tag. One app cannot settle whether the scan-to-unlock pattern holds without a sponsor behind the scanned item, or whether it is a form the sponsorship takes. What would settle it is a second app in which the scanned item is the product's own rather than a sponsor's, and scanning it grants an in-product benefit under a repeat limit. The per-item versus per-category limit was also not settled in this session.

system.tagline: A digital sticker album for the FIFA World Cup where every source of stickers, scanning, daily claims, purchases, converges on one held pack count, and registering through FIFA.com raises every allowance at once.
system.overview: FIFA Panini Collection channels every way of getting stickers, scanning physical products, a daily free pack, sign-up bonuses, challenge rewards and a paid deluxe pack, into one held count of unopened packs, with a daily allowance governing only how many can be opened rather than how many can be held. Registering through a FIFA.com account raises that allowance and several others at once rather than unlocking features one at a time. Duplicates route to a swap stack matched against other users by the app itself, and a private team of friends layers a second swap scope and a public profile on top of the same album.
system.loop: Packs enter a held count from scanning, a daily claim, sign-up, promo codes, challenge rewards and deluxe pack purchases. Opening one resolves into players; missing ones glue into the album and advance its completion, feeding the achievement badges, the challenges' collect-N conditions and the public profile's own figures, while duplicates go to a swap stack and into swap requests the app matches on its own. A daily allowance limits opening to one pack for a guest and four for a registered account, and a separate cap limits how many swap requests can run at once. Registration through FIFA.com raises both figures together, along with unlocking challenges, teams and promo codes. The $2 deluxe pack and two purchase-count rewards are the only paid entries, both eventually converging on a keepsake album sold outside the app, and the whole collection stops being available on 30 September 2026.
system.keyInsight: Registration is the one action that raises nearly every capacity in the system at once: the pack-opening allowance, the swap-request cap, and access to challenges, teams and promo codes all move together the moment a FIFA.com account is linked, rather than unlocking one at a time. The account choice screen states every one of these allowances as an exact number before the user picks a route, so the trade a guest is making is fully quantified before they decide.
system.whatMakesItWork: Every route into the system, scanning a product, claiming a daily pack, completing a challenge or paying for a deluxe pack, resolves into the same held count of packs, so adding a new acquisition source costs the system nothing structurally: it just adds another way to fill a count the rest of the loop already knows how to spend. The one place this convergence breaks is the swap system, which the app matches on its own rather than letting the user browse for a partner, and whose own resolution, what happens the moment a match is found, was never actually shown.

roles.role: An album with one slot per player recognizes completion at more than one level at once, the whole album and its cosmic-sticker subset separately, each with its own named reward.
Packs held as a count resolve into different players on opening, and the $2 deluxe pack guarantees categories of stickers without naming which ones.
A daily allowance caps pack opening at one for a guest and four registered, stated to return in 15 hours; a separately stated, less-confirmed cap limits open swap requests.
A free pack is granted for a single tap, once a day, at a higher rate for a registered account.
Three numbered challenges each state a target, a reward and an end date, staying visible after they expire.
A tiered badge page names criteria across collecting, swapping, challenges and a sponsor's own scanned products.
A named team of up to ten friends, joined by ID and password, unlocks a private swap scope and shows each member's own completion.
Two rewards sit at fixed counts of deluxe packs purchased, both positions and their contents shown before any purchase is made.

connections.title: Opened packs feed the album
connections.desc: Each opened pack resolves into players, and any that are missing from the album get glued into their own slot.
connections.effect: The album's completion depends entirely on what the loot box resolves to, not on a separate acquisition step.

connections.title: The daily allowance limits how many packs get opened
connections.desc: Pack opening is capped at one a day for a guest and four for a registered account, stated to return in 15 hours.
connections.effect: The rate stickers can enter the album is set by the opening allowance, not by how many packs are held.

connections.title: The daily free pack is itself an unopened pack
connections.desc: The daily grant adds one pack to the same held count that scanning, sign-up and challenges also feed.
connections.effect: The daily login reward has no separate resolution of its own; it just adds another entry to the loot box's held count.

connections.title: Challenges require stickers already glued into the album
connections.desc: A sticker must be in the album and clicked before it counts toward a challenge's progress.
connections.effect: Challenge progress is downstream of album progress, not a separate track running alongside it.

connections.title: Album completion advances the badge tiers
connections.desc: Album progress, teams completed and swap counts are all read directly off the same album and profile state the achievement badges track.
connections.effect: The achievement system adds no state of its own; it recognizes points already reached on the album.

connections.title: Completed challenges are their own badge tier
connections.desc: Challenges completed is one of the seven achievement categories, tiered at one, three and five.
connections.effect: A challenge's reward and its contribution to a badge tier are earned by the same completion, not two separate systems.

connections.title: Team members' own completion is read off the same album state
connections.desc: The team page shows each member's completion, drawn from the same percentage the public profile states for an individual.
connections.effect: The team adds no separate progress measure; it surfaces the same album state for more than one person at once.

connections.title: Each purchase toward the ladder is itself a deluxe pack
connections.desc: The count of deluxe packs purchased, which the ladder's two rewards key off, rises with the same purchase that opens a deluxe loot box.
connections.effect: Progress toward the ladder's rewards and opening another loot box are the same action, not two separate spends.
